problem: The fix for S3R-hook-runner-C1-1 made a command substitution invisible when an arithmetic span shares its word. _read_word assigns 'subst = _arithmetic_nests_substitution(...)' instead of OR-ing it in, so a '$(' or backtick that comes earlier in the same word is forgotten. And _own_opacity skips any argument that contains '$((' anywhere. So 'echo $(rm -rf /tmp/x)$((1+2))', 'echo "$(id)$((1))"', 'echo `id`$((1))', 'X=$(id)$((1)) ls' and 'echo > $(id)$((1))' now all parse as not opaque. Before this round they were opaque. The form '$((cmd) )' is also not opaque, and sh and bash run it as a command substitution ('sh -c "echo $((echo hi) )"' prints hi). Through the runner, an agent's Bash call 'vsdd survey $(echo pwned > /dev/null)$((1))' gets the caller marker and permissionDecision 'allow' with updatedInput, and so does 'vsdd survey $((echo pwned) )'. HD8 says the decision sent with the rewrite approves the whole command, so the command may hold nothing else. Here it approves an arbitrary command substitution without a prompt for agents and in auto or bypassPermissions mode. No test covers a substitution and an arithmetic span in one word.
proposed_resolution: In _read_word, OR the arithmetic result into subst in both the bare and the double-quoted path ('subst = subst or _arithmetic_nests_substitution(...)'). In _own_opacity, drop the per-argument '$((' exclusion and rely on the word's subst flag. Or remove only the arithmetic spans that nest nothing before looking for '$(' or a backtick. Treat a '$((' span that does not close with '))' as a command substitution (sh and bash run '$((cmd) )'). The simplest safe form: an arithmetic span counts as harmless only when it closes with '))' and its inner text uses only arithmetic characters (digits, names, $name, operators, blanks, parentheses). Add to test_shell.py the opaque cases 'echo $(id)$((1))', 'echo "$(id)$((1))"', 'echo `id`$((1))', 'X=$(id)$((1)) ls', 'echo > $(id)$((1))' and 'vsdd survey $((id) )'. Add a runner test in test_caller.py: an agent's 'vsdd survey $(id)$((1))' gets no marker and no decision. While there: a '${...}' span holding '$(' sets no subst, so 'X=${y:-$(id)} ls' and 'echo > ${y:-$(id)}' are not opaque either. That gap is older than this round. Arguments are covered by _own_opacity, but the program word, assignment values and redirect targets are not.
